In Part A you worked with a **table** of amniotes: one row per species, no
structure between the rows. But those species are not an unordered bag:
every one of them sits on a family tree that connects it, through shared
ancestors, to every other living thing. This part is about that tree: how
it is stored as data, how to draw it three ways (rectangular, round, and
against a time axis), and what the words biologists use for it (*clade*,
*ancestor*, *divergence*) mean on the screen.

Note what changed and why. Part A's amniote table (Myhrvold et al. 2015)
stores **traits**, and its nested taxonomy columns (class, order, family,
genus) do encode a tree: nesting is a hierarchy. But it is a tree of
*named ranks*: it carries no dates, and inside every rank it is silent.
The table can say that fifteen families belong to the primates without
saying anything about how those families relate to one another. The trees
on this page store what the table cannot: **resolved relationships with
dates**, and not a single measurement. Same animals, complementary data
structures, different sources. All three trees come from
[TimeTree](https://timetree.org) (Kumar et al. 2022), one of them the
family tree of exactly the amniotes whose traits you analysed in Part A,
and below we will draw the table's tree and TimeTree's side by side:

| File | Tips | What one tip is |
|---|---|---|
| `amniotes_family.nwk` | 956 | one family of amniotes (mammals, birds, reptiles) |
| `eukaryotes_class.nwk` | 235 | one class of eukaryotes: animals, fungi, plants, protists |
| `eukaryotes_phylum.nwk` | 66 | one phylum of eukaryotes |

All code runs in your browser. The first cell may take a few seconds while
Python loads.

```{pyodide}

plt.rcParams.update({

    "axes.spines.top": False,
```

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
#| include: false
# Pre-build every name the page uses, so each cell works no matter which
# cells were run before it. The visible cells re-derive all of this.
class Node:
    def __init__(self, name="", length=0.0):
        self.name = name
        self.length = length
        self.children = []
        self.parent = None
    def is_leaf(self):
        return not self.children
    def leaves(self):
        return [self] if self.is_leaf() else [l for c in self.children for l in c.leaves()]
    def walk(self):
        yield self
        for c in self.children:
            yield from c.walk()

def parse_newick(text):
    s = text.strip().rstrip(";")
    pos = 0
    def read_label():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == "'":
            end = s.index("'", pos + 1)
            label, pos_ = s[pos + 1:end], end + 1
        else:
            start = pos
            pos_ = pos
            while pos_ < len(s) and s[pos_] not in ",():;":
                pos_ += 1
            label = s[start:pos_]
        pos = pos_
        return label.strip()
    def read_length():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == ":":
            pos += 1
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",();":
                pos += 1
            return float(s[start:pos])
        return 0.0
    def read_node():
        nonlocal pos
        node = Node()
        if s[pos] == "(":
            pos += 1
            while True:
                child = read_node()
                child.parent = node
                node.children.append(child)
                if s[pos] != ",":
                    break
                pos += 1
            pos += 1
        node.name = read_label()
        node.length = read_length()
        return node
    return read_node()

def set_depths(root):
    for node in root.walk():
        node.depth = (node.parent.depth if node.parent else 0.0) + node.length

def layout(root):
    set_depths(root)
    for i, leaf in enumerate(root.leaves()):
        leaf.y = float(i)
    def place(node):
        if not node.is_leaf():
            for c in node.children:
                place(c)
            node.y = sum(c.y for c in node.children) / len(node.children)
    place(root)

def draw_tree(root, ax, colors=None, default="#555555", lw=0.8,
              labels=False, fontsize=6):
    layout(root)
    segs = {}
    def add(col, x0, y0, x1, y1):
        xs, ys = segs.setdefault(col, ([], []))
        xs += [x0, x1, None]; ys += [y0, y1, None]
    for node in root.walk():
        col = (colors or {}).get(id(node), default)
        if node.parent:
            add(col, node.parent.depth, node.y, node.depth, node.y)
        if not node.is_leaf():
            ys = [c.y for c in node.children]
            add(col, node.depth, min(ys), node.depth, max(ys))
    for col, (xs, ys) in segs.items():
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=col, lw=lw, solid_capstyle="round")
    if labels:
        for leaf in root.leaves():
            col = (colors or {}).get(id(leaf), "#222222")
            ax.text(leaf.depth, leaf.y, " " + leaf.name, va="center",
                    fontsize=fontsize, color=col)
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for side in ("left", "top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)

def draw_round(root, ax, colors=None, default="#555555", lw=0.7,
               labels=False, fontsize=5, gap_deg=10):
    layout(root)
    tips = root.leaves()
    max_d = max(t.depth for t in tips)
    span = np.deg2rad(360 - gap_deg)
    a0 = np.deg2rad(90 + gap_deg / 2)
    def ang(y):
        return a0 + span * y / max(len(tips) - 1, 1)
    segs = {}
    def add(col, pts):
        xs, ys = segs.setdefault(col, ([], []))
        xs += [p[0] for p in pts] + [None]; ys += [p[1] for p in pts] + [None]
    for node in root.walk():
        col = (colors or {}).get(id(node), default)
        if node.parent:
            add(col, [(ang(node.y), node.parent.depth), (ang(node.y), node.depth)])
        if not node.is_leaf():
            ys = sorted(c.y for c in node.children)
            arc = np.linspace(ang(ys[0]), ang(ys[-1]), 24)
            add(col, list(zip(arc, np.full(24, node.depth))))
    for col, (xs, ys) in segs.items():
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=col, lw=lw, solid_capstyle="round")
    if labels:
        for t in tips:
            a = ang(t.y); deg = np.rad2deg(a) % 360
            flip = 90 < deg < 270
            ax.text(a, max_d * 1.02, t.name,
                    rotation=(deg + 180 if flip else deg), rotation_mode="anchor",
                    ha="right" if flip else "left", va="center", fontsize=fontsize,
                    color=(colors or {}).get(id(t), "#222222"))
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines["polar"].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(False)

def clade(root, names):
    want = set(names)
    best = None
    for node in root.walk():
        have = {l.name for l in node.leaves()}
        if want <= have and (best is None or len(have) < len(best[0])):
            best = (have, node)
    return best[1] if best else None

def paint(groups):
    colors = {}
    for cl, col in groups:
        for node in cl.walk():
            colors[id(node)] = col
    return colors

mini = parse_newick("((Homo:6.7, Pan:6.7):2.2, Gorilla:8.9);")
set_depths(mini)

amniotes = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "amniotes_family.nwk").read())
set_depths(amniotes)
root_age = max(l.depth for l in amniotes.leaves())
primates = clade(amniotes, ["Hominidae", "Lemuridae"])

amniote_rows = [line.split(",") for line in
                open_url(DATA_URL + "amniote_species.csv").read().strip().split("\n")[1:]]
primate_families = sorted({r[2] for r in amniote_rows if r[1] == "Primates"})

euk = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "eukaryotes_class.nwk").read())
set_depths(euk)
euk_age = max(l.depth for l in euk.leaves())
animals = clade(euk, ["Mammalia", "Demospongiae"])
fungi   = clade(euk, ["Agaricomycetes", "Chytridiomycetes-1"])
plants  = clade(euk, ["Magnoliopsida", "Chlorophyceae"])
colors = paint([(animals, "#4269d0"), (fungi, "#e66852"), (plants, "#30a8b1")])

phyla = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "eukaryotes_phylum.nwk").read())
set_depths(phyla)
phyla_age = max(l.depth for l in phyla.leaves())
```

## 1 · Reading a phylogenetic tree

A phylogenetic tree has three kinds of parts, and each one asserts
something:

- **Tips** (leaves) are observed things: living species, families,
  classes. They are the only part anyone has ever seen.
- **Internal nodes** are inferred ancestors: "these two lineages were once
  one population." Nobody has seen one; each is a hypothesis.
- **Branch lengths**, in the trees on this page, are **time**: a branch of
  length 6.7 means 6.7 million years of independent evolution.

Where do the trees come from? Mostly from genetics. Take the same gene
from many species, line the DNA sequences up, and count differences:
mutations accumulate roughly steadily, so more differences means more time
since two lineages separated. That gives the *shape* and *relative* ages.
To turn relative ages into millions of years, the tree is calibrated
against fossils whose age and position are known. TimeTree, the source of
our files, aggregates thousands of such published studies into consensus
dated trees, which is why every tree here comes with real ages attached.

## 2 · The Newick format

Before we can draw a tree we need it as data. The standard format,
**Newick**, writes a tree as nested parentheses: each pair of parentheses
is one internal node (one ancestor), and `:number` after a name is the
branch length. Here is one you can read by eye: humans, chimps and
gorillas, with TimeTree's ages in millions of years (Myr):

```
((Homo:6.7, Pan:6.7):2.2, Gorilla:8.9);
```

Read from the inside out: `Homo` and `Pan` each sit at the end of a
6.7-Myr branch from their shared ancestor, so the human–chimp split was
6.7 million years ago. That ancestor connects, 2.2 Myr further back, to
the ancestor it shares with `Gorilla`: 6.7 + 2.2 = 8.9 Myr, exactly
`Gorilla`'s own branch length. In a dated tree every tip is the same total
distance from the root, because every living lineage has had the same
amount of time.

The format is recursive (a tree is a node whose children are trees), so
the parser is recursive too. This is the only genuinely fiddly code on the
page; read it, run it, and then it is just a function we call:

```{pyodide}
class Node:
    def __init__(self, name="", length=0.0):
        self.name = name          # taxon name (tips) or support label (internal)
        self.length = length      # branch length to the parent, in Myr here
        self.children = []        # empty list = this node is a tip
        self.parent = None

    def is_leaf(self):
        return not self.children

    def leaves(self):
        return [self] if self.is_leaf() else [l for c in self.children for l in c.leaves()]

    def walk(self):
        yield self
        for c in self.children:
            yield from c.walk()


def parse_newick(text):
    s = text.strip().rstrip(";")
    pos = 0

    def read_label():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == "'":            # quoted label, e.g. '90'
            end = s.index("'", pos + 1)
            label, pos = s[pos + 1:end], end + 1
        else:
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",():;":
                pos += 1
            label = s[start:pos]
        return label.strip()

    def read_length():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == ":":            # ":6.7" = branch length
            pos += 1
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",();":
                pos += 1
            return float(s[start:pos])
        return 0.0

    def read_node():
        nonlocal pos
        node = Node()
        if s[pos] == "(":                             # "(" = ancestor: recurse
            pos += 1
            while True:
                child = read_node()
                child.parent = node
                node.children.append(child)
                if s[pos] != ",":
                    break
                pos += 1
            pos += 1                                  # consume ")"
        node.name = read_label()
        node.length = read_length()
        return node

    return read_node()


mini = parse_newick("((Homo:6.7, Pan:6.7):2.2, Gorilla:8.9);")
print("tips:", [l.name for l in mini.leaves()])
```

```{pyodide}
assert [l.name for l in mini.leaves()] == ["Homo", "Pan", "Gorilla"]
assert mini.children[0].children[0].name == "Homo"
assert mini.children[0].children[0].length == 6.7
print("✓ parser reads tips, structure and branch lengths correctly")
```

## 3 · Drawing the tree

To draw a tree we give every node two coordinates. **x** is its total
distance from the root: add branch lengths from the root down, which for
a dated tree means x *is* time. **y** spreads the tips out one per row,
and each ancestor sits at the mean of its children:

```{pyodide}
def set_depths(root):
    for node in root.walk():
        node.depth = (node.parent.depth if node.parent else 0.0) + node.length


def layout(root):
    set_depths(root)
    for i, leaf in enumerate(root.leaves()):
        leaf.y = float(i)
    def place(node):
        if not node.is_leaf():
            for c in node.children:
                place(c)
            node.y = sum(c.y for c in node.children) / len(node.children)
    place(root)


def draw_tree(root, ax, colors=None, default="#555555", lw=0.8,
              labels=False, fontsize=6):
    layout(root)
    segs = {}                     # colour -> one long broken line
    def add(col, x0, y0, x1, y1):
        xs, ys = segs.setdefault(col, ([], []))
        xs += [x0, x1, None]; ys += [y0, y1, None]
    for node in root.walk():
        col = (colors or {}).get(id(node), default)
        if node.parent:                                   # horizontal branch
            add(col, node.parent.depth, node.y, node.depth, node.y)
        if not node.is_leaf():                            # vertical connector
            ys = [c.y for c in node.children]
            add(col, node.depth, min(ys), node.depth, max(ys))
    for col, (xs, ys) in segs.items():
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=col, lw=lw, solid_capstyle="round")
    if labels:
        for leaf in root.leaves():
            col = (colors or {}).get(id(leaf), "#222222")
            ax.text(leaf.depth, leaf.y, " " + leaf.name, va="center",
                    fontsize=fontsize, color=col)
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for side in ("left", "top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)


fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 2.4))
draw_tree(mini, ax, labels=True, fontsize=11)
ax.set_xlabel("Myr since the root")
plt.show()
```

(One drawing trick worth stealing: instead of one `ax.plot` per branch,
thousands of tiny artists, we collect all segments of a colour into a
single line broken by `None` gaps and draw it in one call. Same picture,
orders of magnitude faster.)

Now a real tree. This is every family of **amniotes**, the same group
whose species table you cleaned in Part A, one level of aggregation up:

```{pyodide}
amniotes = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "amniotes_family.nwk").read())
set_depths(amniotes)
root_age = max(l.depth for l in amniotes.leaves())
print(f"{len(amniotes.leaves())} families, root {root_age:.1f} Myr ago")
```

```{pyodide}
assert len(amniotes.leaves()) == 956
assert round(root_age) == 319
print("✓ 956 amniote families; the amniote common ancestor lived ~319 Myr ago")
```

```{pyodide}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 7))
draw_tree(amniotes, ax, lw=0.4)
ax.set_xlabel("Myr since the amniote root")
ax.set_title(f"All amniotes at family level: {len(amniotes.leaves())} tips, one ancestor")
plt.show()
```

No labels: at 956 tips they would be soup. What the shape alone shows:
every mammal, bird and reptile family traces back to **one node** ~319 Myr
ago, and the big early fork you can see near the root is mammals splitting
from the reptile-plus-bird lineage. That number is not decoration; you
will meet it again below, coming from a completely different file.

## 4 · Clades and common ancestors

A **clade** is an ancestor plus *all* of its descendants: a complete
subtree, snapped off at one internal node. "Mammals" is a clade;
"cold-blooded animals" is not, because their common ancestor also has
warm-blooded descendants. Clades are the only groups a tree can actually
point at, and the way to find one is through the **MRCA**, the most
recent common ancestor of some tips you name:

```{pyodide}
def clade(root, names):
    """Smallest clade whose tips include every name in `names` (their MRCA)."""
    want = set(names)
    best = None
    for node in root.walk():
        have = {l.name for l in node.leaves()}
        if want <= have and (best is None or len(have) < len(best[0])):
            best = (have, node)
    return best[1] if best else None


primates = clade(amniotes, ["Hominidae", "Lemuridae"])
print(f"{len(primates.leaves())} families, crown age "
      f"{root_age - primates.depth:.1f} Myr")
```

Name two primate families and you get all of Primates, every family
descended from the same ancestor, ~74 Myr ago:

```{pyodide}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.6))
draw_tree(primates, ax, labels=True, fontsize=9, default="#4269d0")
ax.set_xlabel("Myr since the amniote root")
ax.set_title("The primate clade, cut from the amniote tree")
plt.show()
```

```{pyodide}
assert len(primates.leaves()) == 19
assert round(root_age - primates.depth) == 74
print("✓ 19 primate families from one ancestor ~74 Myr ago")
```

Look at the tips before moving on: `Hominidae` (all great apes,
including you) is one twig among nineteen. And `Paleopropithecidae`, the
sloth lemurs, are **extinct**: humans reached Madagascar roughly two
thousand years ago, and the last sloth lemurs disappeared around 500
years ago. A dated tree can carry recently-lost lineages alongside
living ones, though nothing in the drawing itself marks them as gone.

### Taxonomy columns versus a phylogeny

A fair objection: Part A's amniote table has class, order, family and
genus columns, and that nesting *is* a tree. True, so let us build it.
Take every primate family in the life-history table and hang it off one
node, which is exactly the structure the columns encode, then draw it
next to the TimeTree primate clade:

```{pyodide}
text = open_url(DATA_URL + "amniote_species.csv").read()
rows = [line.split(",") for line in text.strip().split("\n")[1:]]
primate_families = sorted({r[2] for r in rows if r[1] == "Primates"})

star = Node("Primates")
for name in primate_families:
    tip = Node(name, length=1.0)
    tip.parent = star
    star.children.append(tip)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 5.5))
draw_tree(star, axes[0], labels=True, fontsize=9)
axes[0].set_title(f"Part A's taxonomy: {len(primate_families)} families, one node")
axes[0].set_xticks([])
draw_tree(primates, axes[1], labels=True, fontsize=9, default="#4269d0")
axes[1].set_title("TimeTree: the same clade, resolved and dated")
axes[1].set_xlabel("Myr since the amniote root")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The left tree is real, but look at what it knows. Every family attaches
directly to the order: one giant **polytomy**, because the table records
membership, not relatedness, and its branch lengths mean nothing. The
right tree makes claims the left cannot: apes split from monkeys before
either split from lemurs, and every split has a date. Rank nesting gives
you a tree of *names*; a phylogeny gives you a tree of *events*.

```{pyodide}
tree_names = {l.name.split("-")[0] for l in primates.leaves()}
assert len(primate_families) == 15
assert "Indridae" in primate_families and "Indriidae" in tree_names
assert "Paleopropithecidae" in tree_names and "Paleopropithecidae" not in primate_families
print("✓ 15 families in the table, 16 in the tree, and the mismatches teach:")
print("  Indridae vs Indriidae is the same family spelled two ways by two")
print("  databases, and the extinct sloth lemurs cannot appear in a table")
print("  of measured life histories")
```

Even the family *lists* disagree between the two sources: a one-letter
spelling drift and an extinct lineage. Whenever two databases must be
joined on names, this is the normal condition, not the exception.

### Your turn: the carnivore clade {#sec-ex-carnivora}

Cats and dogs are both carnivorans. Extract the clade containing
**Canidae** (dogs) and **Felidae** (cats), draw it with labels, and print
how many families it holds and how long ago their common ancestor lived.

```{pyodide}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: ex_carnivora
import js
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pyodide.http import open_url

DATA_URL = js.location.href.split("site_libs/")[0] + "data/"

class Node:
    def __init__(self, name="", length=0.0):
        self.name = name
        self.length = length
        self.children = []
        self.parent = None
    def is_leaf(self):
        return not self.children
    def leaves(self):
        return [self] if self.is_leaf() else [l for c in self.children for l in c.leaves()]
    def walk(self):
        yield self
        for c in self.children:
            yield from c.walk()

def parse_newick(text):
    s = text.strip().rstrip(";")
    pos = 0
    def read_label():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == "'":
            end = s.index("'", pos + 1)
            label, pos = s[pos + 1:end], end + 1
        else:
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",():;":
                pos += 1
            label = s[start:pos]
        return label.strip()
    def read_length():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == ":":
            pos += 1
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",();":
                pos += 1
            return float(s[start:pos])
        return 0.0
    def read_node():
        nonlocal pos
        node = Node()
        if s[pos] == "(":
            pos += 1
            while True:
                child = read_node()
                child.parent = node
                node.children.append(child)
                if s[pos] != ",":
                    break
                pos += 1
            pos += 1
        node.name = read_label()
        node.length = read_length()
        return node
    return read_node()

def set_depths(root):
    for node in root.walk():
        node.depth = (node.parent.depth if node.parent else 0.0) + node.length

def layout(root):
    set_depths(root)

              labels=False, fontsize=6):
    layout(root)
    segs = {}
    def add(col, x0, y0, x1, y1):
        xs, ys = segs.setdefault(col, ([], []))
        xs += [x0, x1, None]; ys += [y0, y1, None]
    for node in root.walk():
        col = (colors or {}).get(id(node), default)
        if node.parent:
            add(col, node.parent.depth, node.y, node.depth, node.y)
        if not node.is_leaf():
            ys = [c.y for c in node.children]
            add(col, node.depth, min(ys), node.depth, max(ys))
    for col, (xs, ys) in segs.items():
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=col, lw=lw, solid_capstyle="round")
    if labels:
        for leaf in root.leaves():
            col = (colors or {}).get(id(leaf), "#222222")
            ax.text(leaf.depth, leaf.y, " " + leaf.name, va="center",
                    fontsize=fontsize, color=col)
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for side in ("left", "top", "right"):
        ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)

def clade(root, names):
    want = set(names)
    best = None
    for node in root.walk():
        have = {l.name for l in node.leaves()}
        if want <= have and (best is None or len(have) < len(best[0])):
            best = (have, node)
    return best[1] if best else None

plt.rcParams.update({
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.22, "font.size": 11,
})
amniotes = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "amniotes_family.nwk").read())
set_depths(amniotes)
root_age = max(l.depth for l in amniotes.leaves())
```

::: {.solution exercise="ex_carnivora"}
**Fully worked solution:**

```python
carnivora = clade(amniotes, ["Canidae", "Felidae"])

print(f"{len(carnivora.leaves())} families, common ancestor "
      f"{root_age - carnivora.depth:.1f} Myr ago")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
draw_tree(carnivora, ax, labels=True, fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel("Myr since the amniote root")
plt.show()
```

16 families from one ancestor ~55 Myr ago, and the tree answers
questions the table never could. Cats' closest relatives here are the
civets, hyaenas and mongooses, not dogs; dogs sit on the other side of the very
first split, nearer to bears and seals. "Cats and dogs" feel like a
natural pair to us, but the clade says they have been separate lineages
almost since the dinosaurs left.
:::

## 5 · The round tree of life

Rectangular layout runs out of room fast: tips need vertical space, and
at hundreds of tips the picture becomes a wall. The classic fix is to
bend the y-axis into a **circle**: angle becomes tip position, radius
becomes time. Same coordinates, different projection:

```{pyodide}
def draw_round(root, ax, colors=None, default="#555555", lw=0.7,
               labels=False, fontsize=5, gap_deg=10):
    layout(root)
    tips = root.leaves()
    max_d = max(t.depth for t in tips)
    span = np.deg2rad(360 - gap_deg)
    a0 = np.deg2rad(90 + gap_deg / 2)         # leave the gap at the top
    def ang(y):
        return a0 + span * y / max(len(tips) - 1, 1)
    segs = {}
    def add(col, pts):
        xs, ys = segs.setdefault(col, ([], []))
        xs += [p[0] for p in pts] + [None]; ys += [p[1] for p in pts] + [None]
    for node in root.walk():
        col = (colors or {}).get(id(node), default)
        if node.parent:                                   # radial branch
            add(col, [(ang(node.y), node.parent.depth), (ang(node.y), node.depth)])
        if not node.is_leaf():                            # connecting arc
            ys = sorted(c.y for c in node.children)
            arc = np.linspace(ang(ys[0]), ang(ys[-1]), 24)
            add(col, list(zip(arc, np.full(24, node.depth))))
    for col, (xs, ys) in segs.items():
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=col, lw=lw, solid_capstyle="round")
    if labels:
        for t in tips:
            a = ang(t.y); deg = np.rad2deg(a) % 360
            flip = 90 < deg < 270                 # keep left-side labels readable
            ax.text(a, max_d * 1.02, t.name,
                    rotation=(deg + 180 if flip else deg), rotation_mode="anchor",
                    ha="right" if flip else "left", va="center", fontsize=fontsize,
                    color=(colors or {}).get(id(t), "#222222"))
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines["polar"].set_visible(False)
    ax.grid(False)


def paint(groups):
    """groups: list of (clade_root, colour). Returns {id(node): colour}."""
    colors = {}
    for cl, col in groups:
        for node in cl.walk():
            colors[id(node)] = col
    return colors


euk = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "eukaryotes_class.nwk").read())
set_depths(euk)
euk_age = max(l.depth for l in euk.leaves())
print(f"{len(euk.leaves())} classes of eukaryotes, root {euk_age:.0f} Myr ago")
```

```{pyodide}
assert len(euk.leaves()) == 235
assert round(euk_age) == 1598
print("✓ 235 classes; the eukaryote root here is ~1,598 Myr, about 1.6 billion years")
```

We colour three clades (animals, fungi, green plants) by naming two
anchor tips for each, exactly as we did for primates. Everything not in a
painted clade stays grey:

```{pyodide}
animals = clade(euk, ["Mammalia", "Demospongiae"])       # vertebrates .. sponges
fungi   = clade(euk, ["Agaricomycetes", "Chytridiomycetes-1"])
plants  = clade(euk, ["Magnoliopsida", "Chlorophyceae"]) # flowering plants .. green algae

colors = paint([(animals, "#4269d0"), (fungi, "#e66852"), (plants, "#30a8b1")])

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10.5, 10.5))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="polar")
draw_round(euk, ax, colors=colors, default="#9a9a9a", labels=True, fontsize=4.5)

from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
ax.legend(handles=[
    Line2D([], [], color="#4269d0", lw=2.5, label=f"Animals ({len(animals.leaves())})"),
    Line2D([], [], color="#e66852", lw=2.5, label=f"Fungi ({len(fungi.leaves())})"),
    Line2D([], [], color="#30a8b1", lw=2.5, label=f"Green plants ({len(plants.leaves())})"),
    Line2D([], [], color="#9a9a9a", lw=2.5, label="Other eukaryotes"),
], loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(-0.05, 1.05), frameon=False, fontsize=9)
plt.show()
```

```{pyodide}
assert (len(animals.leaves()), len(fungi.leaves()), len(plants.leaves())) == (80, 44, 32)
print("✓ animals: 80 classes, fungi: 44, green plants: 32; and 79 classes in grey")
```

Three things this picture says that a list of species cannot:

- **Everything familiar is a wedge.** All animals (sponges to humans)
  are one blue sector. All of `Mammalia` is a single tick mark.
- **The grey is not filler.** A third of the disc is protists: algae,
  amoebae, ciliates, parasites. "Protist" is not a clade; it is the word
  for *every eukaryote outside the three painted wedges*, and the tree
  shows they do not form one group.
- **Fungi sit next to animals, not plants.** The red and blue wedges
  share an ancestor long after either shared one with plants:
  mushrooms are, genealogically, closer to you than to anything green.

## 6 · The timetree of life

The round tree is for shape; a **timetree** puts the ages back on a
readable axis. We use the phylum-level file (66 tips) and relabel the
x-axis to run backwards from today, with a few reference events:

```{pyodide}
phyla = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "eukaryotes_phylum.nwk").read())
set_depths(phyla)
phyla_age = max(l.depth for l in phyla.leaves())
n = len(phyla.leaves())

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 10))
draw_tree(phyla, ax, labels=True, fontsize=7)
mya = np.array([1500, 1250, 1000, 750, 500, 250, 0])
ax.set_xticks(phyla_age - mya)
ax.set_xticklabels(mya)
ax.set_xlabel("millions of years ago")
for edge, lab in [(539, "Cambrian begins"), (252, "end-Permian extinction"),
                  (66, "end-Cretaceous extinction")]:
    ax.axvline(phyla_age - edge, color="#bbbbbb", lw=0.7, zorder=0)
    ax.text(phyla_age - edge, n - 0.5, " " + lab, fontsize=7, color="#777777",
            rotation=90, ha="right", va="top")
ax.set_xlim(0, phyla_age * 1.30)
plt.show()
```

Almost every animal phylum was already a separate lineage before the
Cambrian began; the famous "explosion" shows up here as a dense burst
of splits just *before* the boundary. (The one split you can see on the
Cambrian side of the line involves `Brachiopoda-3`, an artifact of
TimeTree splitting a group it cannot recover as one clade; see the
serving notes.) And no branch ends at either extinction
line: at phylum level, every lineage on this chart survived both of the
worst catastrophes in the fossil record.

Because branch lengths are time, "when did X and Y split?" is one
subtraction, the root's age minus the depth of the two tips' MRCA:

```{pyodide}
print(f"chordates vs arthropods (us vs insects): "
      f"{phyla_age - clade(phyla, ['Chordata', 'Arthropoda']).depth:.0f} Mya")
print(f"animals vs fungi:  "
      f"{euk_age - clade(euk, ['Mammalia', 'Agaricomycetes']).depth:.0f} Mya")
print(f"animals vs plants: "
      f"{euk_age - clade(euk, ['Mammalia', 'Magnoliopsida']).depth:.0f} Mya")
print(f"animals vs choanoflagellates: "
      f"{euk_age - clade(euk, ['Mammalia', 'Choanoflagellata']).depth:.0f} Mya")
```

```{pyodide}
assert round(euk_age - clade(euk, ["Mammalia", "Agaricomycetes"]).depth) == 1275
assert round(euk_age - clade(euk, ["Mammalia", "Magnoliopsida"]).depth) == 1598
print("✓ the animal–fungus split (1,275 Mya) is younger than the animal–plant "
      "split (1,598 Mya): fungi really are our closer cousins")
```

Notice we just wrote the same subtraction four times, each time reaching
for the right root age by hand. That kind of repetition is code begging
to be packaged into a function, which is exactly the exercise.

The last line above is worth a pause: **choanoflagellates**, single-celled
flagellates that strain bacteria out of water, split from us ~894 Mya;
they are the closest living relatives of all animals, and they look
remarkably like the feeding cells of a sponge.

### Your turn: close the loop {#sec-ex-split}

In Section 3 the amniote family tree put the amniote root at **319 Myr**.
The eukaryote class tree is a completely different file, built from a
different set of studies at a different taxonomic rank, but it contains
`Mammalia` and `Aves` as tips. Write a `divergence(root, a, b)` helper
and use it to date the mammal–bird split in *this* tree, then compare.

```{pyodide}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: ex_split
import js
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pyodide.http import open_url

DATA_URL = js.location.href.split("site_libs/")[0] + "data/"

class Node:
    def __init__(self, name="", length=0.0):
        self.name = name
        self.length = length
        self.children = []
        self.parent = None
    def is_leaf(self):
        return not self.children
    def leaves(self):
        return [self] if self.is_leaf() else [l for c in self.children for l in c.leaves()]
    def walk(self):
        yield self
        for c in self.children:
            yield from c.walk()

def parse_newick(text):
    s = text.strip().rstrip(";")
    pos = 0
    def read_label():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == "'":
            end = s.index("'", pos + 1)
            label, pos = s[pos + 1:end], end + 1
        else:
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",():;":
                pos += 1
            label = s[start:pos]
        return label.strip()
    def read_length():
        nonlocal pos
        if pos < len(s) and s[pos] == ":":
            pos += 1
            start = pos
            while pos < len(s) and s[pos] not in ",();":
                pos += 1
            return float(s[start:pos])
        return 0.0
    def read_node():
        nonlocal pos
        node = Node()
        if s[pos] == "(":
            pos += 1
            while True:
                child = read_node()
                child.parent = node
                node.children.append(child)
                if s[pos] != ",":
                    break
                pos += 1
            pos += 1
        node.name = read_label()
        node.length = read_length()
        return node
    return read_node()

def set_depths(root):
    for node in root.walk():
        node.depth = (node.parent.depth if node.parent else 0.0) + node.length

def clade(root, names):
    want = set(names)
    best = None
    for node in root.walk():
        have = {l.name for l in node.leaves()}
        if want <= have and (best is None or len(have) < len(best[0])):
            best = (have, node)
    return best[1] if best else None

euk = parse_newick(open_url(DATA_URL + "eukaryotes_class.nwk").read())
set_depths(euk)
```

```{pyodide}
split = divergence(euk, "Mammalia", "Aves")
print(f"Mammalia-Aves split in the eukaryote class tree: {split:.1f} Mya")
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex_split"}
**Hint 1**: The split date of two tips is the age of their most recent
common ancestor, and you already have a helper on this page that finds
that node from two names. What it stores is measured *from the root*,
and you want years *before today*.
:::

::: {.hint exercise="ex_split"}
**Hint 2**: In a dated tree, every living tip is the same total
distance from the root, so the root's age is the depth of any tip
(safest: the maximum leaf depth). Age and depth run in opposite
directions.
:::

**How to know you got it.** No solution button here: this function is
yours. If it works, the two printed dates agree *exactly*. Before you
celebrate independent confirmation, ask two questions. First, why is the
mammal–bird split the very same event as the amniote root? Second, both
numbers ultimately came from the same database: what would it actually
take for two dates like these to count as independent evidence?

{{< include _instructor-b.qmd >}}

## What a tree shows and what it does not

Reading a phylogeny is a visual skill worth being pedantic about:

- **Only the nodes and branch lengths carry information.** The vertical
  order of tips is arbitrary: every internal node can be flipped like a
  mobile, so "top of the chart" means nothing. Humans are not "at the
  end" of the tree; every living tip is exactly the same distance from
  the root.
- **The level of aggregation is part of the claim**: the Part A lesson
  again. At phylum level no lineage dies in the great extinctions; at
  family level, recently lost lineages like the sloth lemurs sit in the
  tree beside the living. Same history, different rank, different story.
- **Every internal node is an inference**, and some are genuinely
  contested: whether sponges or comb jellies split from the rest of the
  animals first is a live argument in the literature, and this page's
  files quietly take a side. A drawn tree always looks more certain than
  the science behind it.

## Sources and serving notes

- Kumar et al. (2022) *TimeTree 5: an expanded resource for species
  divergence times*, Molecular Biology and Evolution 39:msac174;
  [timetree.org](https://timetree.org). Trees downloaded via "Build a
  Timetree" (group: Amniota at family rank; Eukaryota at class and phylum
  rank), Newick format, branch lengths in Myr; values unmodified.
- Names with suffixes (`Cebidae-1`, `Cebidae-2`) are TimeTree's way of
  serving groups that its consensus does not recover as single clades:
  the name is split, the tree is left honest.
- Tobias et al. (2022) AVONET and Myhrvold et al. (2015): the Part A
  datasets this page's amniotes connect back to.
